purpose: Source inventory and paraphrased knowledge-base seed notes for personalized visual conversation recommendations.
important_distinction: Human-impression agreement, cue detection and personalized conversation-outcome prediction are different evaluation targets.

sources.title: Nonverbal Communication
sources.finding: Reviews the production, perception and measurement of nonverbal cues across face, voice, body and interpersonal space.
sources.use: Build a cue vocabulary and contextual interpretation rules.
sources.limit: A review, not a validated event-conversation scoring formula.

sources.title: On the Accuracy of Personality Judgment: A Realistic Approach
sources.finding: The Realistic Accuracy Model links accuracy to relevance, availability, detection and appropriate utilization of behavioral cues.
sources.use: Check relevance and observability before interpreting a cue.
sources.limit: Does not establish that any particular event cue predicts conversation enjoyment.

sources.title: Personality Judgments Based on Physical Appearance
sources.finding: Observers' full-body photograph judgments correlated with self/peer criteria for several traits; spontaneous presentation provided broader information than constrained poses.
sources.setting: Full-body photographs with standardized or spontaneous presentation.
sources.use: Motivate joint observation of dress, posture and expression.
sources.limit: Does not establish personalized conversation compatibility or permit treating an individual's appearance as a personality diagnosis.

sources.title: Dress Is a Fundamental Component of Person Perception
sources.finding: Proposes integrating dress, face/body, context and perceiver characteristics, including aesthetic preferences, into person-perception research.
sources.setting: Review of dress and impression formation.
sources.use: Model user-specific aesthetic affinity and contextual dress descriptions.
sources.limit: The organizing categories are proposed, not an empirically derived compatibility scale; impressions are not necessarily accurate.

sources.title: Dominant, Open Nonverbal Displays Are Attractive at Zero-Acquaintance
sources.finding: Expansive posture predicted speed-date interest; experimentally varied postures in dating photographs affected selection.
sources.setting: Speed dating and a dating application.
sources.outcome: Initial romantic interest and partner selection.
sources.use: Include postural expansiveness as an observable candidate feature.
sources.limit: Romantic selection is not evidence of friendly conversation enjoyment; do not infer dominance as an individual's true trait.

sources.title: Giving Men the Come-On: Effect of Eye Contact and Smiling in a Bar Environment
sources.finding: Repeated eye contact combined with smiling produced more approaches than the other tested conditions.
sources.setting: A small bar study involving female confederates and male strangers.
sources.outcome: Whether the stranger approached and spoke.
sources.use: Consider combinations and direction of acknowledgment cues.
sources.limit: Does not establish conversation quality or generalize directly to all genders, cultures or event types.

sources.title: A Recipe for Friendship: Similar Food Consumption Promotes Trust and Cooperation
sources.finding: Assigned similar food consumption increased trust-game behavior and negotiation cooperation relative to dissimilar consumption.
sources.setting: Experimental interactions and judgments involving food.
sources.outcome: Trust and cooperation under the tested conditions.
sources.use: Treat shared consumption as a candidate relational context or conversation hook.
sources.limit: A food item alone does not establish personality, trustworthiness, preference or enjoyable conversation.

sources.title: The Imbibing Idiot Bias: Consuming Alcohol Can Be Hazardous to Your (Perceived) Intelligence
sources.finding: Alcohol cues reduced perceived intelligence without evidence of impaired performance.
sources.use: An example of a cue that affects impressions without demonstrating the inferred attribute.
sources.limit: Never use drink category to infer intelligence, impairment or conversation quality.

sources.title: Thin Slices of Expressive Behavior as Predictors of Interpersonal Consequences: A Meta-Analysis
sources.finding: Brief expressive-behavior judgments were associated with varied social and clinical outcomes; aggregate correlation across 38 results was about .39.
sources.setting: Multiple studies using observations under five minutes.
sources.limit: The aggregate correlation is not classification accuracy or an event-specific compatibility estimate.

sources.title: Emotional Expressions Reconsidered: Challenges to Inferring Emotion From Human Facial Movements
sources.finding: Facial movements vary substantially with context and do not provide a simple universal diagnostic mapping to emotion categories.
sources.setting: Review of facial-movement and emotion research.
sources.use: Separate visible movement from inferred emotional state.
sources.limit: Neither establishes that expressions are meaningless nor validates reading a private emotional state from a face.

sources.title: F-Formation Detection: Individuating Free-Standing Conversational Groups in Images
sources.finding: Models free-standing interaction groups using position and orientation, grounded in the F-formation concept.
sources.use: Describe spatial access and group arrangement.
sources.limit: Detecting a group or a gap does not establish permission to join or future enjoyment.

sources.title: ConfLab: A Data Collection Concept, Dataset, and Benchmark for Machine Analysis of Free-Standing Social Interactions in the Wild
sources.finding: Records a professional networking event with 48 participants and provides benchmarks including speaking activity and group formation.
sources.setting: A conference networking event; overhead video and wearable sensors.
sources.use: Study event annotation and group/behavior measurement.
sources.limit: Not a dataset of personalized conversation satisfaction; camera view differs from first-person footage.

sources.title: First Impressions: A Survey on Vision-Based Apparent Personality Trait Analysis
sources.finding: Reviews vision-based apparent-personality analysis, datasets, subjective labels and methodological limitations.
sources.use: Understand technical approaches and evaluation pitfalls.
sources.limit: Predicting apparent traits is distinct from predicting real personality or conversation outcomes.

sources.title: The Social Psychology of Perceiving Others Accurately
sources.finding: An academic reference on interpersonal accuracy across domains.
sources.use: Knowledge-base foundation for accuracy and observer differences.
sources.limit: Book-level description; retrieve and cite the relevant chapter when making specific empirical claims.

sources.title: Conducting Interaction: Patterns of Behavior in Focused Encounters
sources.finding: Observational studies of gaze, greetings, facial behavior, attention and spatial organization.
sources.use: Develop operational definitions for orientation, greeting and interaction entry.
sources.limit: Not a validated numerical scoring scheme for personalized compatibility.

sources.title: Sequential Analysis and Observational Methods for the Behavioral Sciences
sources.finding: Explains behavioral coding schemes, observer training, reliability and sequential analysis.
sources.use: Design annotations and evaluate coder agreement.
sources.limit: Methodological guidance; does not validate this proposed rubric.

sources.title: Snoop: What Your Stuff Says About You
sources.finding: Accessible account of research on belongings and environments as cues to people.
sources.setting: Personal spaces and possessions; linked edition is a later paperback.
sources.use: Generate hypotheses about chosen objects and self-presentation.
sources.limit: Distinguish accumulated personal environments from an incidental object carried at an event.

sources.title: A Closer Look at First Sight: Social Relations Lens Model Analysis of Personality and Interpersonal Attraction at Zero Acquaintance
sources.local_source: User-supplied Back PDF inspected in the prior session; original not redistributed.
sources.finding: Visible and audible cue factors were associated with aggregate initial liking; observer-preference-to-appearance fit had a small association with unique liking (r=.12).
sources.setting: 73 German psychology freshmen giving introductions averaging 7.49 seconds.
sources.outcome: Initial liking/desire to get acquainted and expected liking; not actual enjoyment.
sources.use: Separate general appeal from personalized style affinity; consult back-2011-cue-evidence.json for verified cue correlations and limitations.
sources.limit: Observational, small cohort, subjective mixed cue factors; no held-out enjoyment prediction. In-sample R-squared .67 is not accuracy.

sources.title: A Meta-Analytic Investigation of the Relation Between Interpersonal Attraction and Enacted Behavior
sources.finding: 309 effect sizes, N=5422, associate attraction with enacted behavior.
sources.limit: Does not validate pre-approach individualized enjoyment prediction.

collection_note: Historical source inventory. Review/status flags are preserved; newer summaries in the Markdown research documents take precedence. This is not a complete inventory of later papers and not a predictor.
